subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should ACP `sessions_spawn` accept OpenClaw skill context, and if so which selection modes, redaction/audit fields, and child-observability guarantees are part of the supported contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing it decides whether trusted OpenClaw skill content may be copied into external harness prompts and how that interacts with existing native/Codex skill contracts.

options.title: Start explicit-only with audit
options.body: Add only an explicit skill-id selector first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata before considering auto/default modes.

options.title: Defer to #95058
options.body: Keep ACP skill injection blocked until the broader native/Codex skill prompt-contract parity issue settles the owning prompt layer and lifetime semantics.

options.title: Keep ACP isolated
options.body: Reject core skill injection and require users to use native harness skills, MCP bridges, or ClawHub/plugin-specific mechanisms instead.

recommendation.title: Start explicit-only with audit
recommendation.body: Add only an explicit skill-id selector first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata before considering auto/default modes.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP thread-bound agent feature history and ACP spawn routing originate with osolmaz's central ACP commit, making them the best available owner signal for the initial contract decision.
